choice: scripts/dock-setup.sh starts the helper with `cmux new-surface --placement dock --pane <page pane>` as a background tab of the page's pane; the helper titles its tab 'Linear server' with an OSC escape; a resume binding lets cmux restart it after a relaunch once the user approves Auto-Restore. scripts/dock_surfaces.py takes a terminal for the server's only when it is titled 'Linear server' or its resume binding (`surface resume show --json`) starts cmux-linear-sidebar; right after opening the tab, dock-setup.sh passes the terminals that existed before (--created-after) and takes the one new terminal. Settings other than the defaults go into the typed command and the resume argv as --port and --refresh-seconds; an unchanged binding is left alone so it keeps its approval. The scripts stop a process on the port only when `ps` shows it runs cmux-linear-sidebar and /api/state answers with app 'cmux-linear-sidebar'.
context: The helper asks the cmux CLI which workspace is selected. With the default automation.socketControlMode cmuxOnly, cmux answers only processes started inside its terminals. A review showed that taking the only terminal beside the page for the server let dock-setup.sh type into, and uninstall.sh close, a user's own shell.
rejected: A launchd agent with socket mode `automation` (any process of the user could drive cmux; the user called a system service overkill); socket mode `password` (unverified effect on agent hooks in cmux terminals); reading cmux's session-restore file instead of the socket (undocumented format); the first layout, with the terminal as a visible Dock section above the page (the user disliked the extra window); treating the only terminal beside the page as the server (a user's shell got the server command typed into it and was closed by uninstall); matching 'cmux-linear-sidebar' anywhere in a binding's command string (agent bindings start with `cd -- '<repo folder>'`, which has the same name); any JSON with "status" on the port as proof of our server (another program could be killed).
title: Run the helper in a Dock terminal tab hidden behind the page, recognized by an explicit marker
